drafted_from: tool:read-a-sent-email's own row (tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: its words, input schema and sample run) and test/read-a-sent-email.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Was my email 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031 delivered?", naming the held key, {"key_name": "resend-api-key-of-my-shop", "email_id": "00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031"}. It runs tool:read-a-sent-email and answers {"id":"00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031","from":"Sender <sender@example.com>","to":["delivered@example.org"],"subject":"Hello","created_at":"2026-11-25 14:45:46.162+00","last_event":"delivered"}
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it reads one email your email-sending account sent and writes nothing.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once, so its key is held in your vault under a name of yours (a key with full access: a sending-only key cannot read emails). The key is never typed into the request.
2. Get the email's id from the answer of the send (tool:send-an-email) or from an email event the account told you.
3. Say to your AI: "Read my sent email <id>", and give the held key's name. It calls tools:run with tool tool:read-a-sent-email and {"key_name": "<that name>", "email_id": "<id>"}.
4. Read last_event: what last happened to the email (sent, delivered, bounced, opened, clicked or complained). The email's body and the key are never shown.

worked_examples.title: An email that was delivered
worked_examples.given: The row's sample run: GET https://api.resend.com/emails/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000031 answering a made-up delivered email. The id and addresses are synthetic.
